subject: Request: Temporary SLO exception for incremental deployment with automatic fallback
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Thompson <eliza@nova-payments.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Incremental deploy plan + temporary SLO exception request

Hi Eliza —

Thanks again for the quick call this morning. As discussed, we plan to roll the 2.1.0 model bundle to your production inference pool using an incremental canary (to minimize regression risk while improving accuracy). Because the canary will intentionally shift a small portion of traffic onto a new kernel path and slightly larger KV cache warming windows, we expect a brief, controlled change to tail latency during the very first hour.

Attached: proposed-canary-playbook.md (detailed steps), nova-security-matrix.pdf.

Summary of the ask: Redwood requests a temporary SLO exception for a 48-hour deployment window to run a staged canary with automatic fallback and version pinning. We will:
- Start at 5% traffic for 1 hour, monitor metrics (latency p50/p95, error rate, token-per-second),
- Move to 15% then 35% over a 6-hour ramp only if thresholds are respected,
- Keep the previous model pinned as an immediate fallback route (0-RTT traffic steering),
- Enable automatic fallback triggers (see thresholds below) which will instantly route traffic back to the pinned version.

Automatic fallback / rollback triggers (proposed):
- error rate increase of >0.5 percentage points sustained for 3 minutes
- p95 latency increase > 300ms above baseline for 5 minutes
- any increase in 5xx gateway errors

Can you confirm whether Nova is OK with a temporary SLO exception under these controls and the attached playbook? Procurement (procurement@nova-payments.com) will likely want the formal SLO exception form filled — I can circulate once engineering signs off.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

From: Eliza Thompson <eliza@nova-payments.com>

Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 12:01:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Incremental deploy plan + temporary SLO exception request

Thanks, Soojin.

Quick questions from our side before I loop in procurement:
1) What is the expected user impact window (minutes/hours) if fallback triggers?
2) Who has the authority to trigger a manual rollback on Redwood's side vs automatic?
3) Will we have real-time dashboards and alerting to our SRE on the canary metric set?

Procurement wants a clear maximum duration for any signed SLO exception (we prefer as short as possible). Also, Samir (our SRE) will want a play-by-play and a runbook he can hand to his on-call.

If you can provide those items I can share with procurement and the SRE team; otherwise we need a technical contact for a short call.

- Eliza

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Incremental deploy plan + temporary SLO exception request — need eng sign-off and playbook confirmation

Hannah / Aditya / Monica — forwarding Eliza's note. She and procurement want firm guardrails and a short maximum duration. I drafted the canary steps above and attached the playbook. Need eng confirmation on:
- precise fallback timing (what is our detection to cutover latency?),
- whether we can guarantee dashboarding and an alert to Nova's SRE (Samir) with <2 minute detection,
- whether pinning the previous model version and enabling 0-RTT traffic steering is possible for instant fallback,
- recommended maximum SLO exception window (I suggested 48 hours to limit contract exposure).

Aditya — can you review the attached proposed-canary-playbook.md and respond with exact thresholds/automation details we can share with Eliza?

Best,
Soojin

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Incremental deploy plan + temporary SLO exception request — need eng sign-off and playbook confirmation

Soojin / Hannah —

Reviewed the playbook. TL;DR: we can support the proposed flow with the following concrete behaviors and limits:

1) Detection & automatic fallback
- Our telemetry pipeline will detect the configured signals within ~90s to 3 minutes depending on sampling; we can set a conservative detection window of 3 minutes for automatic fallback to avoid noisy flaps.
- Once a trigger is met (error rate delta, p95 latency delta, or 5xx spike), traffic is re-routed to the pinned version using our traffic steering plane; the change is applied within ~30s of the decision.

2) Pinning and route guarantees
- We will pin the previous model version as an immutable fallback route and ensure that hot caches are kept for the pinned variant to avoid cold-start latency on fallback.
- For further safety, we'll enable a 'fast-path' quantized fallback variant that has lower latencies (slightly lower quality) if the pinned full-precision model is unavailable during an incident.

3) Ramp and exposure
- Start: 5% for 60 minutes; if OK, increase to 15% for 120 minutes, then 35%. Total ramp window ~6 hours.

4) Thresholds (engineering-proposed)
- Error rate: +0.4 percentage points sustained for 3 minutes
- p95 latency: +250ms sustained for 5 minutes
- 5xx: any sustained increase over baseline for 2 minutes

5) Observability and SRE handoff
- We will grant Nova read-only access to the canary dashboard (Grafana) and configure an on-call alert to Samir's PagerDuty with the same thresholds.

6) Exception duration
- Operationally we recommend limiting the SLO exception to 48 hours (day + buffer) to keep contractual exposure low. If extended testing needed, we can renegotiate.

If this is acceptable I can sign off and Soojin can push the formal SLA exception form + playbook to procurement.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Thompson <eliza@nova-payments.com>, procurement@nova-payments.com
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.p@nova-payments.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Final: SLO exception request & signed playbook (Nova Payments / DF-2027-0743)

Hi Eliza / Procurement team —

Following engineering sign-off (Aditya) we are formally requesting a temporary SLO exception for a 48-hour incremental deploy as described in the attached SLA exception form and the canary playbook. Key commitments:
- Automatic fallback triggers (error rate, p95 latency, 5xx) as described; detection window conservative at 3 minutes, rollback applied within ~30s of decision.
- Model pinning + warmed caches to avoid cold start on fallback.
- Read-only Grafana access and PagerDuty alerts to Samir.
- Initial ramp 5% -> 15% -> 35% with manual go/no-go checks at each stage.

Attached: sla-exception-form.pdf (signed by Redwood POC), proposed-canary-playbook.md, nova-security-matrix.pdf.

Please confirm acceptance of the temporary SLO exception and sign the SLA exception form so we can schedule the deployment in the next available maintenance window. If procurement prefers, I can ingest the signed DocuSign link (we included hubspot deal link below).

Next steps:
- Eliza / Procurement: reply with signed exception or any redlines (target: 48 hours)
- Samir: confirm receipt of Grafana invite and PagerDuty escalation target
- Redwood: schedule maintenance window and publish runbook to Nova's read-only space

Thanks,
